---
title: "Merging the genus tables of several datasets"
output: html_document
params:
  input_dir: "results/amplicon/genus_tables"   # one .tsv per dataset: a Genus column and one column per sample
  out_dir: "results/amplicon"
  collapse: "mean"                             # how rows of the same genus are combined: "mean" (as originally) or "sum"
---

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE)
dir.create(params$out_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
```

```{r merge}
library(dplyr)
# This will read ALL .tsv files in the input folder
file_list <- list.files(params$input_dir, pattern = "\\.tsv$", full.names = TRUE)
# Check which files were found
print(file_list)
stopifnot("no .tsv files found in input_dir" = length(file_list) > 0)
collapse_fun <- match.fun(params$collapse)
# Read and process all files
final_df <- lapply(file_list, function(file) {
  read.table(file, header = TRUE, sep = "\t", check.names = FALSE)
}) %>% 
  bind_rows() %>% 
  replace(is.na(.), 0) %>%
  group_by(Genus) %>%
  summarise(across(where(is.numeric), collapse_fun)) %>%
  ungroup()
final_df <- as.data.frame(final_df)
dim(final_df)
write.csv(final_df, file.path(params$out_dir, "merged_bacteria.csv"), row.names=F)
```
